subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: For Telegram local Bot API migration, should OpenClaw reset/scope update offsets by `apiRoot`, rely on doctor/docs for manual reset, or keep account/token-only offsets and treat endpoint switching as operator-managed?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but persisted offset identity and `400: Logged out` tolerance are compatibility-sensitive runtime policy choices that need maintainer intent and live migration proof.

options.title: Endpoint-aware runtime fix
options.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets when `apiRoot` changes, add a narrow logged-out deleteWebhook tolerance, and require live local Bot API proof.

options.title: Doctor/docs reset only
options.body: Keep runtime account/token offsets unchanged and make `openclaw doctor --fix` or documentation the supported way to reset offsets when switching endpoints.

options.title: Keep current advanced workflow
options.body: Leave local Bot API endpoint migration as operator-managed and document the manual cleanup and cooldown expectations.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-aware runtime fix
recommendation.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets when `apiRoot` changes, add a narrow logged-out deleteWebhook tolerance, and require live local Bot API proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Telegram polling/spool work makes this the closest current owner for the ingress and restart behavior that would need to change.
